root_cause.text: The `mailbox-test` driver reused the same `mbox_chan` object for both `tx_channel` and `rx_channel` in the aliasing/MMIO special case, but its probe/remove cleanup code freed both pointers unconditionally, causing a double-free of the same channel.
root_cause.evidence: The patch adds `tdev->rx_channel != tdev->tx_channel` checks before `mbox_free_channel(tdev->rx_channel)` in both `mbox_test_probe()` and `mbox_test_remove()`, and the commit message explicitly says “The RX channel can be aliased to the TX channel if it has a different MMIO… otherwise a double-free occurs.”

agent_logs.root_cause_candidate: The `mailbox-test` driver reused the same `mbox_chan` object for both `tx_channel` and `rx_channel` in the aliasing/MMIO special case, but its probe/remove cleanup code freed both pointers unconditionally, causing a double-free of the same channel.
agent_logs.evidence_points: The patch adds `tdev->rx_channel != tdev->tx_channel` checks before `mbox_free_channel(tdev->rx_channel)` in both `mbox_test_probe()` and `mbox_test_remove()`, and the commit message explicitly says “The RX channel can be aliased to the TX channel if it has a different MMIO… otherwise a double-free occurs.”

intent_record.intent_summary: Avoid double-freeing the shared RX/TX mailbox channel during probe error cleanup.
intent_record.what: In the error-unwind path of `mbox_test_probe()`, the condition guarding `mbox_free_channel(tdev->rx_channel)` was changed from `if (tdev->rx_channel)` to `if (tdev->rx_channel && tdev->rx_channel != tdev->tx_channel)`.
intent_record.how: This prevents the RX channel from being freed twice when the TX and RX channels refer to the same mailbox channel, avoiding a potential double-free during probe failure cleanup.

intent_record.intent_summary: Avoid double-freeing a shared mailbox channel during device removal.
intent_record.what: In mbox_test_remove(), the condition guarding mbox_free_channel() for tdev->rx_channel was changed from checking only whether rx_channel is non-NULL to additionally requiring rx_channel != tx_channel.
intent_record.how: At runtime, this prevents the driver from freeing the same mailbox channel twice when the transmit and receive channels point to the same object. If tx_channel and rx_channel are shared, only the first free occurs and the second is skipped.

grouping_result.intent: Avoid double-freeing the shared RX/TX mailbox channel during probe error cleanup.
Avoid double-freeing a shared mailbox channel during device removal.

relevance_review.reason: The change directly matches the root cause: it prevents freeing the same shared mailbox channel twice when RX and TX alias to the same object.

The group directly addresses the reported root cause: the mailbox-test driver’s removal cleanup was freeing aliased tx/rx channel pointers unconditionally, and the change is specifically to avoid double-freeing a shared mailbox channel.

candidates.rationale: In the aliasing case, tx_channel and rx_channel could refer to the same mbox_chan object, so freeing tx_channel here and then freeing rx_channel afterward leads to a double-free.
This second unconditional free on the same shared channel object causes the double-free when tx_channel and rx_channel alias each other.
During device removal, freeing tx_channel unconditionally is unsafe when tx_channel and rx_channel point to the same channel, because the later rx_channel free repeats the deallocation.
This unconditional second free is directly responsible for the double-free of the shared mailbox channel in the special aliasing/MMIO case.

vuln_statements.explanation: This unconditional free is vulnerable because in the aliasing/MMIO special case tx_channel and rx_channel can point to the same mbox_chan, so freeing tx_channel and then freeing rx_channel causes a double-free.
This unconditional free is vulnerable because it repeats deallocation of the same shared mbox_chan when tx_channel aliases rx_channel, directly causing the double-free.
